**Questions 6, 7(a), 7(b), 8, 9(a), 9(c) and 9(d) of the 4 February Letter**

[Questions 6 and 8]  
5. As stated in paragraph 9 of the 1st Witness Statement of TANG Wing-wah dated 16 January 2026, I was the officer-in-charge (“**Oic**”) of the first fire appliance that arrived at Wang Fuk Court and was the Incident Commander of the No. 1 Alarm Fire (from 1451 hours to 1501 hours). I understand that there were other first responders involved at the initial stage of the incident and that their witness statements are still in progress of being taken by the Hong Kong Police Force Against such background, I, as the Incident Commander of the initial stage of the fire as well as one of the key first responders, hereby provide response to Question 6. The response should be read together with the timeline and account of the No. 1 Alarm Fire provided in paragraphs 8 to 17 of the 1st Witness Statement of TANG Wing-wah dated 16 January 2026.

6. From 0900 hours on 26 November 2025 to 0900 hours on 27 November 2025, I was on duty at TPFStn, serving as the Watch Commander and Oic of the Hydraulic Platform of TPFStn (“**TP/HP**”).

7. At 1451 hours on 26 November 2025, I received a report of No. 1 Alarm Fire at Wang Cheong House, Wang Fuk Court from the Fire Services Communications Centre (“**FSCC**”). The caller provided information as follows: “fire involving scaffolding on external wall with explosion occurred”. I departed from TPFStn together with the crews of TP/HP including 1 Senior Fireman and 4 Firemen and arrived at Wang Fuk Court at 1456 hours.

8. TP/HP was parked at the roundabout outside the front entrance of Wang Cheong House (i.e. at the north-west side of the block)) (_Layout Plan (1) refers_). Upon arrival at the scene, I did not see any fire or smoke on the façade of Wang Cheong House facing Kwong Wang Street and nearby buildings.
